notesStmt.note: This manuscript must have been produced between 1889 and 1890, as the note written on the reverse indicates that Whitman received the envelope in 1889 and the poem to which the line in this manuscript contributed, "A Twilight Song," was published in 1890.

"A Twilight Song: For unknown buried soldiers, North and South" was first published in the May 1890 issue of Century Illustrated Monthly Magazine. With minor changes and without the subtitle, it was included in Good-Bye My Fancy (1891) and in the "Good-Bye My Fancy" annex to Leaves of Grass (1891-1892).

A flash of love—
an —a special
hour for
yel you—
each name recall'd ‸by me from the
darkness
